diagnoses.summary: High SPE with coherent shift dominated by CSTR H2 vent and pressure signals; most consistent with a fault in the H2 PCV path causing restricted venting and pressure buildup.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations, driven by hydrogen vent (PCV) related abnormalities and reactor pressure rise. The top rule-based hypothesis points to the H2 PCV being stuck closed, with capacity degradation also plausible.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violated. Evidence points to the H2 PCV subsystem being the root cause, with the reactor pressure signal also stressed. The most likely faults are related to the H2 PCV valve performance, possibly followed by PCV degradation or a sensor bias contributing to the observed pressure indication.
Coherent process upset with high pressure and hydrogen vent anomaly pointing to H2 PCV/vent valve issue propagating through the reactor system.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with significant pressure-related manifestations, dominated by hydrogen vent dynamics. Evidence points to a faulty H2 PCV (vent valve) affecting reactor pressure control.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violations. Strong evidence points to an H2 vent (PCV) abnormality driving reactor pressure up, with the top contributors dominated by CSTR H2 vent flow and TOP_TIC response.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong pressure rise and H2 vent involvement; likely a fault in the H2 PCV path causing reactor pressure to elevate and vent flow to mis-match controller actions.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with concurrent high T2 and SPE, strongly pointing to a H2 vent pathway issue (H2 PCV). The top contributing measurements point to the H2 vent and related control actions driving the upset, along with elevated reactor and top-tray temperatures. Likely multiple faults affecting the H2 PCV and related pressure/flow paths.
High plant movement with simultaneous SPE and T² violations, aligned with a stuck H2 vent valve reducing venting and causing reactor pressure rise.
Most likely a hydrogen vent (PCV) / H2 handling fault causing reactor pressure rise and abnormal correlations; PCV fault is driving the upset and cooling/condenser effects are secondary.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous high T² and high SPE, alarms on reactor pressure, and saturated control loop. The most consistent fault is an H2 PCV issue propagating pressure rise, with possible condenser-related damping loss and a saturated RB_LIC loop.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong SPE signals across multiple process variables, consistent with a condenser cooling effectiveness loss propagating through the column and related sections. Additional weaker indicators point to possible H2 PCV issues and an RB_LIC constraint contributing to the upset.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violations, pointing to multiple interacting faults centered on the CSTR vent (H2 PCV) and condenser/cooling path, with additional pressure sensor and RB_LIC behavior contributing to the trend.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong SPE violations and multiple alarmed variables; top contributors point to PCV and condenser-related faults amid saturated control loops and rising reactor/feed pressures.

PCA shows a large coherent plant upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and an active DIST_X_L alarm. The leading fault hypotheses point to condenser cooling and an RB_LIC-related issue, with possible secondary contributions from reboiler/leakage dynamics.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with strong distillate acetone signal and elevated reboiler/cold-end indicators; several faults can explain the abnormal correlations, with condenser cooling loss being the most consistent with the DIST_X_L alarm and the observed contributor pattern.

PCA detects a large, coherent upset with strong distillate acetone deviation and multiple downstream temperatures affected; high T2 and SPE indicate a significant, propagating fault rather than random sensor noise. Rule-based hints point to condenser cooling loss as the primary issue, with RB_LIC operating at its PV but saturated (out of range), and potential reboiler liquid behavior anomalies.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong distillate acetone signaling and an active DIST_X_L alarm. The highest-weighted fault hypothesis is a condenser cooling effectiveness issue causing abnormal distillate composition and column dynamics, with a secondary possibility of the RB_LIC loop saturating (out-of-range) and a minor contribution from reboiler liquid leak.

PCA abnormal with large coherent movement (high T2) and strong SPE violation; strongest evidence points to loss of condenser cooling effectiveness affecting the column, with secondary effects causing RB_LIC saturation and related outlet control issues.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with strong indicators in distillation hardware and condenser performance. The strongest rule-based hint is condenser cooling loss causing column pressure and temperature deviations, with a saturated RB_LIC loop and an out-of-spec distillate acetone reading.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and a distillate acetone signal; multiple elevated tray temperatures and a high distillate acetone measurement point to an issue propagating through the column. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling effectiveness loss, with secondary considerations of RB_LIC being out of range and reflux flow/stiction affecting the reflux path.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations, with the strongest rule-based hint pointing to condenser cooling loss as the root cause, supported by downstream disturbances (distillate acetone alarm, tray temperatures). Saturated RB_LIC loop also suggests up-stream control effort or an out-of-range signal contributing to the upset.

PCA detects a large, coherent upset with strong distortion in key tray temperatures and distillate acetone composition, consistent with condenser cooling effectiveness loss causing abnormal condenser/column behavior and distillate quality alarm. Upstream loop is compensating (tight control on TOP_TIC); RB_LIC appears saturated, pointing to a constraint or actuator issue downstream. Likely multiple faults staged, but condenser cooling loss is the primary driver.

A large, coherent plant upset with strong SPE contamination points to a condenser cooling issue driving distillate composition anomaly and column pressure rise; RB_LIC saturation is secondary evidence. The most likely fault is condenser cooling effectiveness loss.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong SPE and T² violations, consistent with a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness driving abnormal column behavior and distillate quality alarm.

A large, coherent process upset with condenser cooling being less effective, causing high column pressure and upset in the distillation train. The most likely fault is condenser cooling loss, with secondary possibilities of loop output saturation (R_LIC/RB_LIC) and related valve/stiction or feed/overflow issues.

The PCA shows a large coherent upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and an active DIST_x_L alarm in the distillation system, with multiple feed/loop actuators saturated. The rule-based evidence points most strongly to degraded condenser cooling performance driving the distillation disturbance.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by tray-temperature measurements and a distillate acetone alarm, with saturated control loops on LICs. This points to a condenser cooling issue propagating through the column and distillate stream.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with strong SPE; the strongest rule-based hypothesis is condenser cooling loss, consistent with an abnormal distillate x acetone alarm and the major contributors being multiple tray temperature measurements that align with a condenser-related disturbance.

A large, coherent plant upset with saturated control loops and a strong contribution from condenser-related variables; high T² and high SPE indicate a process-wide disturbance with a likely change in condenser cooling effectiveness, consistent with a condenser cooling loss impacting the column and distillate stream.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with widespread drive of tray temperatures and distillate alarm, consistent with condenser cooling loss causing insufficient condensation and abnormal column operation; multiple control loops are saturated as they attempt to compensate. Condenser cooling loss is the most likely fault. Other plausible simultaneous faults are related to H2 PCV issues and CSTR outlet/cold-feed disturbances, but condenser cooling loss best explains the observed pattern.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations, with the most contributing measurements pointing to the condenser cooling path. The active alarms and saturated control loops support a condenser cooling effectiveness fault leading to high column pressure and disturbed distillate composition.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations and DIST_X_L alarm active. Likely condenser cooling effectiveness is degraded, causing the column to heat up and distillate acetone quality to drop, with multiple heat-transfer loops running against setpoints.

PCA detects a large, coherent process upset with strong SPE (abnormal correlations), dominated by tray temperature measurements and signs of condenser/proximate distillation disturbances. The fixed-rule hypotheses favor a condenser cooling loss driving a high-pressure/distillate imbalance, with possible upstream valve/pump saturation contributing to the observed saturation in several loops.

PCA shows a coherent but large upset with simultaneous high T² and high SPE, with condenser-related symptoms and saturated control loops. The rule-based hypotheses favor condenser cooling loss as the primary fault, with additional potential PCV/flow regulation issues contributing to the upset.

High Hotelling T2 and SPE with coherent plant movement and multiple saturated PI loops; DISTILLATE aluminum/acetone imbalance plus column/ condenser control saturations point to a condenser cooling issue propagating through the column and distillate stream.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violations and multiple saturated loops, with distillate composition alarm and column tray indicators. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling loss affecting the column condenser, driving abnormal column behavior and triggering downstream saturations and distillate issues.

PCA signals a large, coherent upset with multiple loops saturated and an active condenser-related alarm; most likely condenser cooling effectiveness loss causing column pressure rise and distillate composition alarms.

Abnormal PCA move with both high Hotelling T2 and high SPE, dominated by a large, coherent disturbance. Most likely a condenser cooling effectiveness loss affecting the column, with secondary upsets in upstream valve/controller loops.

Abnormal PCA with very large T2 and SPE indicates a coherent process upset with new correlations arising in the column/condenser area. The most consistent fault is condenser cooling loss, causing reduced heat rejection and driving column temperature/pressure up and distillate quality issues.

Abnormal PCA: large coherent process upset with multiple loop saturations and strong contribution from tray temps; most likely a condenser cooling effectiveness loss causing abnormal column behavior and downstream flow control saturation.

PCA abnormal state with large, coherent movement (high T²) and large SPE violation; multiple loops saturated with PVs at setpoints, plus distillate acetone alarm. Most consistent with a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness driving column disturbances and downstream alarms.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations; DIST_X_L alarm and several saturated control loops point to a condenser/cooling issue propagating through the column. The most likely root cause is condenser cooling loss, with secondary possibilities related to upstream/outlet control and H2 vent behavior.

A large, coherent plant upset with high Hotelling T² and high SPE, with saturated control loops and an alarm on the distillate line, most consistent with condenser cooling effectiveness loss driving abnormal column behavior and subsequent loop saturation.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations. The most plausible immediate causes are condenser cooling loss driving abnormal column behavior, with downstream actuator saturations (COL_PIC, DR_LIC) and a possible reflux-drum condition contributing to the disturbance.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong SPE violations and saturated control loops. The top evidence points to a loss of condenser cooling performance driving distillate/column disturbances and holdup shifts, with reflux drum leakage also plausible given drum holdup and alarms. Likely multiple faults none excluding others.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with strong contribution from the reflux drum holdup and associated control loops, with a high Hotelling T2 and high SPE pointing toward a process disturbance near the reflux drum. The active alarms and saturated loops support a leak/flow issue in the reflux drum path.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with significant dissociation between correlations (high T² and high SPE), with drum-related signals dominating. The strongest rule-based hypothesis is a leak in the reflux drum, supported by drum holdup changes and column tray alarms, with upstream control loops saturated as they attempt to compensate.

High T2 with high SPE due to a coherent process upset centered on the reflux drum; strongest evidence supports a leak in the reflux drum liquid line causing mass balance disturbance and triggering column tray alarms.
